output: {"answers":{"v02":"Precision and recall grade the same search from two directions. Search 'jaguar' returns 10 pages: 8 are about the car, 2 about the animal, and the index actually holds 20 car pages. Precision answers 'of what I returned, how much was relevant': 8/10 = 0.8. Recall answers 'of all relevant pages, how many did I find': 8/20 = 0.4. Loosen the filter to return 30 pages and recall might climb to 0.95 while precision falls — the two usually trade off. Which one matters depends on the cost of each mistake: a spam filter needs high precision (never delete real mail), a cancer screen needs high recall (never miss a case). So judge any search, flagging, or screening result by asking both questions separately; one blended 'accuracy' number hides the difference.","v07":"路灯是典型的公共物品：没法只让交钱的人享受（非排他），一个人用也不减少别人的光亮（非竞争）。这带来一个麻烦——小区要装路灯，每户都知道无论自己出不出钱，只要别人凑够，自己照样受益。于是理性的选择是装穷，等别人掏钱：这就是搭便车。人人都这么想，钱就凑不齐，路灯修不成——不是大家不需要，而是收益收不回付费者手里。所以公共物品常靠税收和公共预算供给，而不是市场。判断依据：看到「人人都想享受、没人愿意出钱」的现象，就往公共物品上想。条件一变结论也变：能收费就不同了，有线电视能对不付费者断信号，市场就能供给得很好；无线电视收不了费，只能靠广告或公共拨款。","v05":"熵衡量「平均而言结果有多难猜」，单位是比特。总是正面的硬币熵为 0：闭着眼都能说中，毫无不确定。正常硬币两面各半，熵 1 比特，最难猜。为什么均匀时最不确定：任何偏离均匀的偏向都是线索——若正面占九成，你每次押正面，十次对九次；偏向越大越好猜。均匀分布没有任何线索，每个结果等可能，你无法比乱猜做得更好，这就是「最不确定」的含义。公式 H=−Σp·log₂p 把这一点量化：把概率拉平熵升高，推向极端熵降低。条件变化：结果变多，均匀时熵也升高——均匀骰子约 2.58 比特，高于硬币的 1，因为要区分的可能性更多。迁移到压缩：分布越均匀的数据越难压缩，越偏的越可压缩。","d07":"某地统计发现：冰淇淋卖得越多的月份，溺水人数也越多。能说吃冰淇淋导致溺水吗？不能——背后有共同原因：夏天高温，既让人买冰淇淋，也让人下河游泳。相关只说明两个量一起变；因果要求「改变 A 就会改变 B」。检验办法是固定共同原因：只看气温相同的月份，冰淇淋和溺水的关系就消失了，说明相关来自混杂因素。但别走向另一极端，认为相关永远不是因果——吸烟和肺癌的相关，在控制年龄、职业等因素后依然存在，加上生物学机制，才逐步确立为因果。最可靠的手段是随机对照试验：随机分组把混杂因素摊平，剩下的差异才主要来自干预本身。以后遇到「A 和 B 相关」，先找有没有 C 同时导致两者，或 B 导致 A 的可能，再下判断。","d04":"Opportunity cost is the value of the best thing you give up — which is why a 'free' afternoon isn't free. Say your free afternoon has three options: pick up a shift for $50, study for an exam, or nap. If you choose the nap, the opportunity cost is $50, the single best option you passed up — not $50 plus the studying plus everything else; cost means the next-best alternative only. So the real question is always 'is this worth more than my best alternative?' Change one condition and the answer changes: if no shift is offered this week, napping's cost drops to whatever studying would have earned you. The same logic reaches beyond afternoons: a free concert still costs three hours, and a founder's zero-salary year costs the wage she forgoes. The true price tag of any choice is the best thing you didn't choose.","v04":"An operation is idempotent if running it once or many times leaves the same final state. `SET balance=100` is idempotent; `ADD 1 TO balance` is not — retry it three times and you have added 3. Why distributed systems care: networks lose replies. The client sends 'charge $10', the server charges, but the response drops; the client retries. With a non-idempotent operation, the customer gets charged twice. The standard fix is an idempotency key: attach a unique ID to each request, and the server remembers which IDs it has processed, returning the stored result for duplicates. Change one assumption and the design changes: with guaranteed exactly-once delivery, retries would be safe on their own — but real systems only give you at-least-once, so you make operations safely repeatable instead. This is why payment APIs require idempotency keys, and why PUT is idempotent while POST is not.","d05":"检测挺准，为什么测出阳性后患病的把握却不高？某病患病率 1%，抽 1000 人：10 人患病、990 人健康。灵敏度 90%——10 个病人里 9 个测出阳性；假阳率 5%——990 个健康人中约 50 个也呈阳性。阳性共 59 人，真病人只有 9 个：P(患病|阳性)=9/59≈15%。原因是健康人基数太大，5% 的假阳性被乘出 50 人，把 9 个真病人淹没了。贝叶斯公式做的正是这个换算：P(病|阳)=P(阳|病)×P(病)/P(阳)。注意两个量回答的问题不同：90% 是「病人里多少阳性」，15% 是「阳性里多少病人」，不能混用。条件变化：换成患病率 10% 的高危人群，同一检测下阳性后患病概率升到 2/3——同一台机器，筛的人群不同，结果的可信度完全不同。","d06":"A cache is a fast copy of slow data, and cache invalidation is deciding when that copy has gone stale. A web app keeps its truth in a database, but reading it on every page view is slow, so it caches hot items like a bestseller's price. The catch: when the price changes in the database, the cache still holds the old one, and customers see stale numbers until something fixes it. Two common policies: a TTL expires entries after, say, 60 seconds — simple, but stale for up to a minute; write-through invalidates the key the moment the database changes — fresher, but more wiring. Change the setup and new trouble appears: ten app servers each holding their own cache means updating one leaves nine stale. The hard part is the trade-off — fresher data costs more invalidation machinery — which is why cache invalidation is called one of the two genuinely hard problems in computer science.","v08":"Little's law: L = λW, where L is the average number of items in the system, λ the average arrival rate, and W the average time each item spends in the system. Coffee shop example: 10 customers arrive per minute (λ=10/min), each stays 3 minutes (W=3 min), so on average 30 people are inside (L=30). Intuition: during the 3 minutes one customer stays, 30 more arrive — the store holds a rolling crowd of 30. The law lets you compute whichever quantity is hardest to measure: if you know arrivals and want shorter waits, cap how many are allowed in. Two conditions: it holds for averages in a stable system, where long-run inflow equals outflow and queues aren't growing without bound; and it needs no assumptions about arrival or service distributions — Poisson or otherwise. That distribution-free property is what makes it work across manufacturing, networks, and support queues.","v06":"Deadlock is a cycle of waiting where each party holds what the next one needs. Thread 1 locks file A, then asks for lock B; thread 2 already holds B and asks for A. Each waits forever, and neither ever moves. Four conditions must all hold: resources are exclusively held, holders keep them while waiting for more, nothing can be forcibly taken back, and the waiting forms a circle. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible. The cheapest fix is a global lock order — every thread must acquire A before B — which makes the circular wait unbuildable. Alternatives: acquire all locks at once (breaks hold-and-wait), or timeout-and-release (breaks no-preemption, at the cost of possible thrashing). Diagnosis tip: threads stuck forever with CPU near zero, each blocked on a lock the other holds — dump the lock states and look for the cycle.","d02":"Averages can hide spread: {49, 50, 51} and {0, 50, 100} both average 50 but feel completely different. Variance measures that difference. Recipe: subtract the mean from each number, square the results, and average the squares over all N values. First set: deviations −1, 0, 1; squared 1, 0, 1; variance = 2/3 ≈ 0.67. Second set: deviations −50, 0, 50; squared 2500, 0, 2500; variance = 5000/3 ≈ 1667. Why square? Raw deviations always sum to zero — positive and negative cancel — so they cannot measure spread. Squaring stops the cancellation and, as a side effect, punishes large outliers harder: a deviation of 50 contributes 2500, not 50. The cost is odd units (squared points), so people usually report the square root, the standard deviation, back in original units. 'Population' variance just means you have every member of the group, so you divide by N.","v03":"自然选择不是动物「努力变强」，而是一道筛选程序。它只需要三样东西：个体差异随机存在（同一代长颈鹿，脖子天生有长有短）、差异可以遗传（长脖子的父母更多生出长脖子的后代）、差异影响生存繁殖（树叶长在高处，脖子长的吃得更多、留下更多后代）。结果是下一代种群里长脖子基因的比例升高。关键在方向：变异在出生时就随机发生了，环境不指导、不诱导，只做淘汰——被淘汰的是脖子短的个体，不是它们「没努力」。而且变化发生在种群的比例构成上，个体的脖子一辈子不会变长。条件变化：环境改变，筛选方向随之改变；若某性状没有可遗传的变异，环境再怎么筛选也进化不出来。判断依据：看到「为了适应 X 而进化出 Y」的说法要警惕——进化没有目的，Y 是被留下来的结果，不是被追求的目标。","d03":"正反馈是输出绕一圈回来加强输入的回路。麦克风对着音箱：声音被拾进去、放大、从音箱放出、再进入麦克风——每转一圈都以上一圈的输出为新输入，音量一圈比一圈大，直到啸叫刺耳。放大的机制就在这里：只要每圈增益大于 1，变化是逐圈相乘的，指数式增长。但「正」只描述方向（变化被加强），不描述好坏——好坏是人的评价。恐慌抛售是坏的正反馈：股价跌→有人害怕抛售→跌得更多→更多人抛。复利和口碑传播是好的正反馈：钱生钱、用户带来用户。还有一点必然成立：放大有尽头。音箱功率、市场上的现金总有上限，顶到上限后回路饱和或崩溃。想要稳定靠的是负反馈——恒温器到温度就停，把偏差往回拉。判断一个系统会不会失控，先找有没有输出回头加强输入的圈。","d08":"Compound growth means gains earn gains: each year's return is computed on the new, larger balance, so A = P(1+r)^t. $1000 growing at 7% a year becomes about $7612 after 30 years — not $3100, because every dollar of interest starts earning its own interest. Why the starting amount matters: with the same rate and time, results are exactly proportional to the start — $2000 grows to $15,225, precisely double. But the absolute gap widens dramatically: $1000 at the beginning becomes a $7612 gap at the end, since the larger balance earns larger absolute gains each year, compounding the difference further. Change the rate and the effect is fierce: the rule of 72 says doubling time ≈ 72/r, so at 7% money doubles roughly every decade. The practical read: starting earlier or starting with more doesn't just add to compounding — it multiplies through it.","d01":"似然回答：假定某个假设为真，看到眼前这些数据的可能性有多大。抛硬币 10 次出 9 次正面——若硬币公平，似然是 C(10,9)/2¹⁰≈1%；若正面概率是 0.9，似然约 39%。注意似然是「固定数据、变动假设」下比较的量，它本身不是「这枚硬币九成是偏的」。那个反过来的是后验概率：固定数据，问每个假设现在多大可信。两者不可互换：P(数据|假设) ≠ P(假设|数据)。一个经典对照：某病患病率千分之一，检测准确率 99%，你测出阳性——P(阳|病)=99% 很高，但 P(病|阳) 只有一成上下，因为健康人基数太大，假阳性淹没了真病人。联系两者的就是贝叶斯公式：后验 ∝ 似然 × 先验。似然只是数据提供的证据，必须乘上「假设本身原本多大可能」，才得到你要的后验。","v01":"一个学生把 500 道模拟题的答案全背下来，模拟卷回回满分；高考换了新题，一落千丈。这就是过拟合：模型没有学到规律，只是记住了训练数据，包括其中的噪声和偶然波动。模型越灵活、参数越多，越有能力把训练集里的每个细节都「背」下来，所以复杂模型特别容易过拟合。判断信号很明确：训练数据上表现极好，换一批没见过的数据表现明显变差——这个落差本身就是诊断。应对办法顺理成章：用模型没见过的验证集来挑选模型；数据更多时，真实规律会反复出现而噪声各不相同，硬背就不划算了；或者直接限制模型复杂度。条件变化：若训练数据无限多，背答案无所遁形，过拟合消失——所以关键比值是数据量相对模型复杂度，而不是任何一项单独的大小。"}}
